prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where ground was broken for a new temple in 2021.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country or territory where ground was broken for a new temple in 2021.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and milestones, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: In 2021 ground was broken for 12 temples in 7 countries or territories, the start of construction for each. Tonga and Kenya both broke ground on 11 September 2021, at Neiafu and Nairobi.

answers.name: United States of America
answers.fact: Deseret Peak Utah (15 May 2021); Tallahassee Florida (5 June 2021); Syracuse Utah (12 June 2021); and 3 more.

answers.name: Philippines

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Neiafu Tonga (11 September 2021).

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: Nairobi Kenya (11 September 2021).

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Pago Pago American Samoa (30 October 2021).

answers.name: Cambodia
answers.fact: Phnom Penh Cambodia (18 September 2021).

prompts.display_text: Pin a South American country where a current General Authority Seventy served as a young full-time missionary.
prompts.text_original: Many General Authority Seventies serving as of October 2026 were once young full-time missionaries in South America. Pin a South American country where one of them served, as named in the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, the biographies of current General Authority Seventies name young missions in nine South American countries. Brazil and Chile lead, and the list reaches Bolivia, Uruguay and Venezuela.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Brazil Sao Paulo, Porto Alegre, Recife South and Curitiba missions, among others.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Chile Concepcion, Osorno, Santiago South and Vina del Mar missions, among others.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Argentina Cordoba (Elder Haynie) and Resistencia (Elder Olsen) missions.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: Ecuador Guayaquil Mission (Elder Buckner).

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Peru Lima North Mission (Elder Taylor G. Godoy).

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: Bolivia Cochabamba Mission (Elder Strong).

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Colombia Cali Mission (Elder Ortega).

answers.name: Uruguay
answers.fact: Uruguay Montevideo Mission (Elder Alliaud).

answers.name: Venezuela
answers.fact: Venezuela Caracas Mission (Elder Larreal).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory in Mexico, Central America or the Caribbean where a current Seventy served as a young missionary.
prompts.text_original: Several General Authority Seventies serving as of October 2026 were once young full-time missionaries in Mexico, Central America or the Caribbean. Pin a country or territory there where one of them served, as named in the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, the biographies of current General Authority Seventies name young missions in Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and Jamaica. Elder Kevin G. Brown served in his native Jamaica.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Mexico Hermosillo, Monterrey, Torreon, Tampico and North missions, and Veracruz.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Guatemala Guatemala City Mission (Elder Eyre).

answers.name: Dominican Republic
answers.fact: Dominican Republic Santo Domingo East Mission (Elder Eddy).

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: El Salvador missions (Elders Nash and Cordon).

answers.name: Puerto Rico
answers.fact: Puerto Rico San Juan Mission (Elder Corbitt).

answers.name: Jamaica
answers.fact: Jamaica Kingston Mission (Elder Kevin G. Brown).

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country whose Global Histories chronology records its missionaries leaving when World War I began in 1914.
prompts.text_original: When World War I broke out in 1914, Church leaders released the missionaries serving in continental Europe but left those in Great Britain in place. Pin a European country whose Church Global Histories chronology records its missionaries leaving or being evacuated when the war began.
prompts.citation: Saints vol. 3 ch. 11; Global Histories chronologies
prompts.note: Great Britain does not count: its missionaries stayed. Norway does not either: its chronology records only that fewer were sent.
prompts.summary: At the start of World War I, the First Presidency told European leaders to release German and French missionaries, and mission president Hyrum M. Smith then pulled missionaries out of the rest of continental Europe. Missionaries in Great Britain stayed. Local Saints across the continent led branches and preached on their own until the war ended.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: All North American missionaries left Germany during World War I; local members were called to preach (GH Germany, 1914-1919).

answers.name: France
answers.fact: All missionaries left; the French Mission was absorbed, August 1914.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: Full-time missionaries were evacuated from Belgium during the war (GH Belgium, 1914-18).

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: All missionaries evacuated, August 1914.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Mission president told to release all missionaries, August 30, 1914.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Missionaries not native to Denmark sent home, October 1914.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: Missionaries serving in the Netherlands were reassigned to safer missions (GH Netherlands, 1914-19).

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Missionaries from the United States left Sweden in October 1914; local Saints took over the branches.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: All missionaries evacuated, August 10, 1914.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: Missionary work discontinued in 1914.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: Last missionary in Brasso (Brasov) left after the war began.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country where a current Seventy served as a missionary or mission leader (October 2026).
prompts.text_original: As of October 2026, several General Authority Seventies had served as young missionaries or as mission leaders in Africa. Pin an African country where one of their missions was headquartered, as named in the Church's official biographies.
prompts.summary: Africa is now a training ground for Church leaders. As of October 2026, current Seventies had served or presided in missions based in nine African countries, from Nigeria and Ghana to Angola, Mozambique and Benin. Elder Edward Dube served both as a young missionary and as a mission president in his native Zimbabwe.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Lagos and Port Harcourt missionaries (Egbo, Morrison); Enugu and Calabar mission presidents (Chigbundu, Egbo).

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: Elder Isaac K. Morrison presided over the Ghana Cape Coast Mission.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Elder Matswagothata served in the Cape Town mission; Elder Dunn led the Johannesburg mission.

answers.name: Ivory Coast
answers.fact: Elder Thierry K. Mutombo served in the Cote d'Ivoire Abidjan Mission.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Elder Alfred Kyungu presided over the Mbuji-Mayi mission, 2016 to 2019.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: Elder Edward Dube: young missionary in Zimbabwe, later president of the Zimbabwe Harare Mission.

answers.name: Mozambique
answers.fact: Elder Joni L. Koch presided over the Mozambique Maputo Mission.

answers.name: Angola
answers.fact: Elder Denelson Silva presided over the Angola Luanda Mission.

answers.name: Benin
answers.fact: Elder D. Martin Goury presided over the Benin Cotonou Mission.
